LAB-01 // WAZUH TELEMETRYANALYSIS
  • Detected 1/8SMB brute force (T1110)

    Eight NetExec attempts produced 13 authentication-failure alerts (Event ID 4625), correlated by default rule 60204 at level 10.

  • Not detected 3/8Nmap scan, T1082, T1547.001

    The agent reads standard OS event logs only, Windows Firewall logging was off and Sysmon was not installed, so the Nmap scan left nothing to alert on. System information discovery (T1082) and the registry Run key (T1547.001) were not caught by the default ruleset.

  • Did not run 3/8Execution, credential access, defense evasion

    T1059.001, T1003.001 and T1070.001 never ran, so they say nothing about detection. An external payload was missing for the Mimikatz test, ProcDump was unavailable for the LSASS dump, and the log-clearing test was not in the Atomic Red Team version used. These are gaps in my test setup, kept apart from true negatives.

  • Not applicable 1/8Create Account (T1136.001)

    The Atomic Red Team library had no Windows tests for this technique.

About

Second-year Information Systems student at Telkom University. I built a hybrid Wazuh SOC lab and wrote down what the default rules missed. I also write up pentest labs and co-authored a paper on AI coding-agent security.

About

I attack my own labs, watch what Wazuh catches, and write down what it misses.

I am a second-year Information Systems student at Telkom University. I am interested in SOC operations first, then cloud security. Everything on this site comes from labs I built and reports I wrote.

Experience

  1. Sep – Oct 2026

    Research Assistant Intern

    Cyber Security Division, MBC Lab · Telkom University

    • Selected as a Research Assistant Intern after completing the lab's competitive LAS recruitment program.
    • Co-authored the manuscript “Detonating the Rules” with two teammates. It presents RuleDetonate, a four-stage pre-use checker for dependency-hijacking instructions in AI coding-agent rule files. It detects 26.2% of redirected files at a 5% false-positive rate, versus at most 7.8% for general-purpose prompt-injection detectors (3.4×).
    • The benchmark (829 test files) is released openly on Kaggle ↗.
